definition: Accretion means slow growth in which each new layer bonds onto the whole.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word accretion. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know accretion should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Core samples show the glacier grew by accretion, each winter's snowfall pressed into one more thin band of ice atop the last.
An increase is any gain at all — a jump, a spike, a windfall; accretion is the patient kind, growth so slow you only see it by looking back.
An accumulation piles things up but leaves them a pile; accretion goes further — each addition bonds to the body of the thing, the way drip after drip becomes solid stone.

A buildup is any gathering over time — traffic, dust, tension — and the word says nothing about the pieces joining. Accretion makes the stronger claim: each new layer bonds onto the whole, so the thing itself grows. Every accretion is a buildup, but most buildups stay a loose crowd of parts.

Expansion is growth outward in size, scope, or reach, and nothing new has to be added for it — a gas expands, an empire expands. Accretion is the opposite mechanism: the thing grows only because new material keeps arriving and bonding on, addition by addition.
